global_behaviors: For pages backed by authorization_required=true endpoints, include user_id in requests.
Optionally preflight access with POST /customers/{customerId}/log-viewer-authorizations/check before rendering protected data pages.
Show customer-scoped navigation to Requests, Execution Steps, Policy Comparisons, Dashboards, Policy Definitions, Logging Configuration.
Do not expose UI for purge execution, user administration, or LLM insights because the API contract does not provide those capabilities.

pages.title: Execution Requests
pages.purpose: Search and filter request-level execution records over a date range, inspect high-level outcomes and metrics, and drill into one request's audit trail.
data_requirements: Authorized user status for current user/customer.
Request search results with filters: date range, status, final outcome, policy/version, channel, source system, tags, payload field filters, pagination token if available.

api_endpoints.usage: Optional preflight before first protected search or when customer/user context changes.
Primary data source for request grid.

Load next page only if next_page_token is returned
loading_states: Loading next page of request results.
error_states: 403 forbidden: show access denied state with no data grid.
400 invalid request: show inline validation for required date range and supported filters.
Empty results: show no matching requests state.
Network/server error: show retry banner while preserving filters.

pages.title: Request Audit Trail
pages.purpose: Display the full ordered audit trail for a single request, including request/response payloads, overall outcome, and all execution-step details needed for investigation.
data_requirements: Authorized user status for current user/customer.

Request audit trail fetched by request_id from route. API also supports correlation_id, but route is request-based; correlation lookup can be supported from search entry or alternate search control on page.

api_endpoints.usage: Optional preflight before loading protected request details.
Primary source for request header, payloads, and ordered execution_steps.

Optionally fetch by correlation ID through a search field on the page
error_states: 403 forbidden: show access denied state.
404 request not found: show identifier-specific not found message.
400 invalid request: prompt user to provide request or correlation identifier and user context.
Partial-data warning is not applicable because the API returns a single combined object; if request fails, show full-page error.

data_constraints_and_limitations: Search payload filters support only operator 'eq' because that is the only operator exposed by the API contract.
Protected pages require user_id in query/body; frontend must supply it from current user context.
Pagination may be first-page-only in this POV even though next_page_token exists in contract notes; UI should gracefully disable/load no more when token is null.
There is no endpoint for deleting/purging logs, viewing purge job history, exporting reports, saving dashboard presets, or generating LLM insights/recommendations.

There is no endpoint for listing or managing admin/log-viewer users beyond editing allowed_log_viewer_user_ids in customer configuration; display those IDs as raw identifiers rather than assumed user profiles.
There is no endpoint to list distinct policy versions per policy except via listPolicyDefinitions; frontend should derive selectable versions by grouping returned items client-side.
There is no generic request lookup by correlation ID route besides getRequestAuditTrail; correlation-ID searches should use that endpoint directly rather than assuming a list endpoint supports it.
Authentication itself is out of scope; frontend assumes user_id/customer context is already available from host application/session.
